rule_text.name: 701.74a
rule_text.rule: To submerge a card, exile it face up, then put it onto the battlefield face down under its owner's control as a 2/2 face-down creature card with no text, no name, no subtypes, and no mana cost. That permanent is a submerged permanent as long as it remains face down. The effect defining its characteristics works while the card is face down and ends when it’s turned face up.

rule_text.name: 701.74b
rule_text.rule: Unlike manifest, a submerged card can not turn face up again on its own.

rule_text.name: 701.75a
rule_text.rule: To post a bounty on a permanent means to put a bounty counter on that permanent. For as long as that permanent has a bounty counter on it, it has “When this permanent is put into a graveyard from the battlefield, each opponent draws a card.”

rule_text.name: 701.75b
rule_text.rule: A new triggered ability is gained each time a bounty is placed on a permanent.

rule_text.name: 701.75c
rule_text.rule: The permanent will only gain the ability once per time a bounty is posted, even if it would get more than one bounty counter from it, such as through Doubling Season.

rule_text.name: 701.75d
rule_text.rule: If some bounty counters are removed but not all of them, the permanent will still have the ability as many times as a bounty was posted on it.

rule_text.name: 701.80a
rule_text.rule: Conjure is a keyword action. “Conjure (number) cards named (name) to (zone)” means “Put (number) cards named (name) into (zone).”

rule_text.name: 701.80b
rule_text.rule: “Conjure (number) of a random (quality) card to (zone)” means “Put (number) cards of a single (quality) card chosen at random into (zone).”

rule_text.name: 701.80c
rule_text.rule: “Conjure a random (quality) card to (zone) (number) times” means “Repeat this process (number) times. Put a (quality) card chosen at random into (zone)”

rule_text.name: 701.80d
rule_text.rule: To “conjure a duplicate” of an object, conjure the card that has the same name, alternative name, interchangeable name, or name of back face as that object. If such a card does not exist, for example, it is a token named after its types, no card will be conjured.

rule_text.name: 701.80e
rule_text.rule: Conjured cards are not moved from any zone or a player's sideboard.

rule_text.name: 701.80f
rule_text.rule: Conjured cards are cards and not tokens, even if they are represented by token or checklists cards.

rule_text.name: 701.80g
rule_text.rule: Conjured cards are known to all players, even if they are conjured to a hidden zone.

rule_text.name: 701.80h
rule_text.rule: The owner of a conjured card is the player who conjured it, regardless of who controlled the effect that caused that player to conjure it.

rule_text.name: 701.80i
rule_text.rule: When a game ends, cards that were conjured during that game are removed from decks.

rule_text.name: 701.80j
rule_text.rule: When a game is restarted, cards that were conjured during that game remain in decks.

rule_text.name: 701.84a
rule_text.rule: To substantiate a card, put it onto the battlefield face down under your control as a 2/2 face-down creature card with no text, no name, no subtypes, and no mana cost. That permanent is a substantiated permanent as long as it remains face down. The effect defining its characteristics works while the card is face down and ends when it’s turned face up.

rule_text.name: 701.84b
rule_text.rule: Any time you have priority, you may exile and cast a substantiated permanent you control face up. This is a special action that doesn’t use the stack (see rule 116.2b). To do this, show all players that the card representing that permanent is a noncreature card, then cast that card. You still pay its costs, but this is not an alternate cost, so alternate costs can be paid. The effect defining its characteristics while it was face down ends, and it regains its normal characteristics. (If the card representing that permanent is a creature card, it doesn’t have a mana cost, or you are unable to cast it, it can’t be turned face up this way.)

rule_text.rule: To substantiate a card, put it onto the battlefield face down under your control as a 2/2 face-down creature card with no text, no name, no subtypes, and no mana cost. That permanent is a substantiated permanent as long as it remains face down. The effect defining its characteristics works while the card is face down and ends when it’s turned face up.

rule_text.name: 701.84b
rule_text.rule: Any time you have priority, you may exile and cast a substantiated permanent you control face up. This is a special action that doesn’t use the stack (see rule 116.2b). To do this, show all players that the card representing that permanent is a noncreature card, then cast that card. You still pay its costs, but this is not an alternate cost, so alternate costs can be paid. The effect defining its characteristics while it was face down ends, and it regains its normal characteristics. (If the card representing that permanent is a creature card, it doesn’t have a mana cost, or you are unable to cast it, it can’t be turned face up this way.)

mechanics.original_reminder: If you don't control an autocrat, put X +1/+1 counters on this. It becomes an autocrat until it has no +1/+1 counters on it.

rule_text.name: 701.99a
rule_text.rule: “Autocrat N” means “If you don’t control an autocrat, put X +1/+1 counters on this. It becomes an autocrat until it has no +1/+1 counters on it.”

rule_text.name: 701.99b
rule_text.rule: “An autocrat” is a designation that has no rules meaning other than to act as a marker that the autocrat action and other spells and abilities can identify. Only permanents can be or become an autocrat. Once a permanent becomes an autocrat, it stays an autocrat until it leaves the battlefield or has no +1/+1 counters on it. Being an autocrat is neither an ability nor part of the permanent’s copiable values.

rule_text.name: 701.99c
rule_text.rule: If a permanent’s ability instructs a player to “autocrat X,” other abilities of that permanent may also refer to X. The value of X in those abilities is equal to the value of X as that permanent became an autocrat.

rule_text.name: 702.193b
rule_text.rule: If a permanent has multiple instances of alpha, each works separately.

rule_text.name: 702.193c
rule_text.rule: If an alpha permanent loses its +1/+1 counter, it's still alpha and can still only attack alone.

rule_text.name: 702.193d
rule_text.rule: Alpha is a designation that has no rules meaning other than to act as a marker that the alpha abilities and other spells and abilities can identify. Only permanents can be or become alpha. Once a permanent becomes alpha, it stays alpha until it leaves the battlefield. Alpha is neither an ability nor part of the permanent’s copiable values.

rule_text.name: 702.199a
rule_text.rule: Fabled appears on some instants and sorceries with a single target. It represents a static ability while the spell with fabled is on the stack and a spell ability. “Fabled (cost)” means “You may pay (cost) rather than pay this spell's mana cost as you cast this spell.” and “If this spell's fabled cost was paid, and this spell is a double-faced card with an Aura that can enchant that permanent or player as its back face, put this card onto the battlefield transformed and attached to it.”

rule_text.name: 702.199b
rule_text.rule: The fabled ability is linked to an ability printed on its front face that targets one or more objects that can be legally enchanted by its back face. If there are multiple possible targets, one is chosen as the spell with Fable resolves.

rule_text.name: 702.199c
rule_text.rule: If the targeted permanent or player is an illegal target for the Aura side of a card with fabled, such as a creature with protection from enchantments, the card with fabled will not enter the battlefield and instead be put directly into its owner's graveyard from the stack.

rule_text.name: 702.199a
rule_text.rule: Fabled appears on some instants and sorceries with a single target. It represents a static ability while the spell with fabled is on the stack and a spell ability. “Fabled (cost)” means “You may pay (cost) rather than pay this spell's mana cost as you cast this spell.” and “If this spell's fabled cost was paid, and this spell is a double-faced card with an Aura that can enchant that permanent or player as its back face, put this card onto the battlefield transformed and attached to it.”

rule_text.name: 702.199b
rule_text.rule: The fabled ability is linked to an ability printed on its front face that targets one or more objects that can be legally enchanted by its back face. If there are multiple possible targets, one is chosen as the spell with Fable resolves.

rule_text.name: 702.199c
rule_text.rule: If the targeted permanent or player is an illegal target for the Aura side of a card with fabled, such as a creature with protection from enchantments, the card with fabled will not enter the battlefield and instead be put directly into its owner's graveyard from the stack.

rule_text.name: 702.204a
rule_text.rule: Prophecy is a keyword that represents a static ability linked to a triggered ability. “Prophecy (cost)” means “As you reveal this card from a hidden zone, you may exile it if you haven't exiled any cards with their prophecy ability this turn.” and “When you exile this card with its prophecy ability, you may cast it for (cost) rather than paying its mana cost as long as it remains exiled.”

rule_text.name: 702.204b
rule_text.rule:
When a card with prophecy is revealed, any relevant information about it is retained, but the card is exiled and becomes a new object.
Example Cursed Scroll will know the name of a card with prophecy, but it can't be put into a Fact or Fiction pile or chosen during the resolution of Gifts Ungiven.

rule_text.name: 702.204c
rule_text.rule: A card can't be cast for its prophecy cost if it was exiled by an effect other than its prophecy ability.

rule_text.name: 702.208a
rule_text.rule: Shimmer is a triggered ability that may create one or more delayed triggered abilities. “Shimmer” means “Whenever this creature attacks, create a tapped and attacking token that’s a copy of it.” and “Exile that token at the beginning of the end step.”

rule_text.name: 702.208b
rule_text.rule: If a creature has multiple instances of shimmer, each triggers separately.

rule_text.name: 702.208c
rule_text.rule: The delayed trigger will retrigger at every end step. If the trigger is countered, or avoided by ending the turn, the token will remain on the battlefield and the ability will trigger on the next end step.

rule_text.name: 702.208d
rule_text.rule: Shimmer will only exile tokens created by its ability. Replacement effects such as Doubling Season cause shimmer to create two tokens, and both will be exiled. Effects that create a copy of those tokens, such as populate, will create a token will not attempt to be exiled every end step.

rule_text.name: 702.208e
rule_text.rule: If shimmer creates multiple tokens, each one will have its own end step exile trigger.

rule_text.name: 702.208b
rule_text.rule: If a creature has multiple instances of shimmer, each triggers separately.

rule_text.name: 702.208c
rule_text.rule: The delayed trigger will retrigger at every end step. If the trigger is countered, or avoided by ending the turn, the token will remain on the battlefield and the ability will trigger on the next end step.

rule_text.name: 702.208d
rule_text.rule: Shimmer will only exile tokens created by its ability. Replacement effects such as Doubling Season cause shimmer to create two tokens, and both will be exiled. Effects that create a copy of those tokens, such as populate, will create a token will not attempt to be exiled every end step.

rule_text.name: 702.208e
rule_text.rule: If shimmer creates multiple tokens, each one will have its own end step exile trigger.

mechanics.original_reminder: This creature must be blocked each combat if able.

rule_text.name: 702.213a
rule_text.rule: Engage is a static ability of some creatures. “Engage” means “This creature must be blocked each combat if able.”

rule_text.name: 702.213b
rule_text.rule:
This gets difficult when paired with menace. If there are multiple requirements on how creatures can block, the maximum amount of requirements must be obeyed.
Example: Untouched Duelist has engage and menace. You attack with an Untouched Duelist and two creatures with engage. Your opponent has two creatures. Blocking only the Untouched Duelist would leave two unfilled requirements, while blocking the other two engage creatures would leave one unfilled requirement, so the other two engage creatures must be blocked.

rule_text.name: 702.215b
rule_text.rule: The spell with primal is still cast. It is not a special action, it only counts as playing a land when determining if a player can play a land this turn.

rule_text.name: 702.215c
rule_text.rule: A spell can be cast for its primal cost at any point during a player's turn, as long as the number of lands that player can play this turn is greater than the number of lands they have already played this turn, even if timing restrictions would normally prevent playing a land. This means a spell may be cast for its primal cost during its owner's upkeep or end step, but not during another player's turn, or during a turn where lands can't be played.

rule_text.name: 702.215d
rule_text.rule: Additional land plays allow you to play additional cards for their primal cost.

rule_text.name: 702.219a
rule_text.rule: Archive is a static ability of Study enchantments. “Archive X” means “As this permanent enters, shuffle the top X cards of your starting library into an additional, face up, library.”

rule_text.name: 702.219b
rule_text.rule: The additional library is referred to as “the archived library” by the Study with the archive ability that created it.

rule_text.name: 702.219c
rule_text.rule: Whenever state-based actions are checked, if a Study enchantment has an archived library of zero cards, its controller sacrifices it.

rule_text.name: 702.219d
rule_text.rule: If a card would be put into an archived library, that card is put in that library face up.

rule_text.name: 702.219e
rule_text.rule: If a Study card with archive leaves the battlefield, the archived library remains, but is no longer affected by any effects the Study provided.

rule_text.name: 702.219f
rule_text.rule: Cards are not revealed when they are put into a face up library. Cards can still become revealed even though the cards are already visible.

rule_text.name: 702.219g
rule_text.rule: If another player gains control of a Study, they will control any effects of the Study, but will not own the archived library. This means cards from the archived library can't go into that player's hand, graveyard, or library, and cards that player owns can't be put into the archived library. Effects of the Study may still allow them to manipulate or play the cards in that library.

rule_text.name: 702.219h
rule_text.rule: “Your archived libraries” refers to each of your additional libraries that is currently the archived library of a Study on the battlefield. A library still counts as one of your archived libraries if you no longer control the Study, as long as the same object has remained on the battlefield.

rule_text.name: 702.219e
rule_text.rule: If a Study card with archive leaves the battlefield, the archived library remains, but is no longer affected by any effects the Study provided.

rule_text.name: 702.219f
rule_text.rule: Cards are not revealed when they are put into a face up library. Cards can still become revealed even though the cards are already visible.

rule_text.name: 702.219g
rule_text.rule: If another player gains control of a Study, they will control any effects of the Study, but will not own the archived library. This means cards from the archived library can't go into that player's hand, graveyard, or library, and cards that player owns can't be put into the archived library. Effects of the Study may still allow them to manipulate or play the cards in that library.

rule_text.name: 702.219h
rule_text.rule: “Your archived libraries” refers to each of your additional libraries that is currently the archived library of a Study on the battlefield. A library still counts as one of your archived libraries if you no longer control the Study, as long as the same object has remained on the battlefield.

rule_text.name: 702.234a
rule_text.rule: Enspirit represents two static abilities, one that functions while the spell with enspirit is on the stack and another that functions both while it's on the stack and while it's on the battlefield. “Enspirit” means “As an additional cost to cast this spell, you may exile a nonenchantment creature you control until this spell is put from the stack into a zone other than the battlefield or the permanent this spell becomes leaves the battlefield” and “If you chose to pay this spell's additional cost, its total cost is reduced by an amount of generic mana equal to the exiled card's mana value.” Paying a spell's enspirit cost follows the rules for paying additional costs in rules 601.2b and 601.2f–h.

rule_text.name: 702.234b
rule_text.rule: The two abilities represented by enspirit are linked. The first ability may also be linked with any number of other abilities printed on the card with enspirit which refer either to “the exiled card” or to cards “exiled with [this object]”. See rule 607, “Linked Abilities.”

rule_text.name: 702.234c
rule_text.rule: You choose which creature to exile as you choose to pay a spell's enspirit cost (see rule 601.2b), and you exile that creature as you pay the total cost (see rule 601.2h).

rule_text.name: 702.234d
rule_text.rule: A creature “becomes enspirited” when it's exiled to pay a spell's enspirit cost. Abilities that trigger when a creature becomes enspirited are leaves-the-battlefield abilities (see rule 603.6c).

rule_text.name: 702.237c
rule_text.rule: Mirror of Possibilities is a colorless Masterpiece artifact token with “Whenever you cast a spell, you may pay {3}. If you do, copy it. You may choose new targets for the copy”

rule_text.name: 702.237d
rule_text.rule: Thrice-Folded Lotus is a colorless Masterpiece artifact token with “{T}: Add three mana of any one color” and “{3}, {T}: Thrice-Folded Lotus deals 3 damage to any target.”

rule_text.name: 702.237e
rule_text.rule: Eureka! checks if you cast a spell this turn when the ability resolves. This means you can cast a spell in response to the trigger to get a counter.

rule_text.name: 702.242a
rule_text.rule: Tether appears on some instants and sorceries. It represents two abilities. The first is a spell ability that functions while the spell with tether is on the stack. The second is a static ability that functions while the card with tether is in the exile zone. “Tether” means “If this spell is represented by a card, you may exile this card tethered to a creature you control” and “When the creature this card is tethered to dies, you may cast this card from exile without paying its mana cost.”

rule_text.name: 702.242b
rule_text.rule: The term “tethered” describes the relationship between the card with tether while in the exile zone and the creature chosen when the spell represented by that card resolves.

rule_text.name: 702.242c
rule_text.rule: The card with tether remains tethered to the chosen creature as long as the card with tether remains exiled and the creature remains on the battlefield. The card remains tethered to that object even if it changes controller or stops being a creature, as long as it remains on the battlefield.

rule_text.name: 702.242d
rule_text.rule: If the permanent is put into a graveyard while not a creature, the 'dies' trigger of tether will still trigger.

rule_text.name: 702.242e
rule_text.rule: Tether to type is a variant of the tether ability. “Tether to [type]” means “If this spell is represented by a card, you may exile this card tethered to a [type] you control” and “When the permanent this card is tethered to is put into a graveyard from the battlefield, you may cast this card from exile without paying its mana cost.”

mechanics.original_reminder: You may have this creature overclock an artifact you control when either enters. If you do, it stops overclocking any other artifacts.

rule_text.name: 702.258a
rule_text.rule: Overclock is a keyword that represents two triggered abilities. “Overclock” means “When this creature enters, if you control both this creature and another artifact, you may overclock another artifact you control for as long as both remain permanents on the battlefield under your control or until this creature overclocks another artifact” and “Whenever an artifact you control enters, if you control both that artifact and this creature, you may overclock this artifact for as long as both remain creatures on the battlefield under your control or until that creature overclocks another artifact.”

rule_text.name: 702.258b
rule_text.rule: An artifact becomes “overclocked” with another as the result of a overclock ability. Abilities may refer to an overclocked artifact, the artifact a creature overclocks, or whether an artifact is overclocked.

rule_text.name: 702.258c
rule_text.rule: A creature can only overclock one artifact, however an artifact may be overclocked by multiple creatures.

rule_text.name: 702.258d
rule_text.rule: An overclocked artifact stops being overclocked if any of the following occur: another player gains control of it or the creature overclocking it; it or the creature overclocking it leaves the battlefield; or the creature overclocking it overclocks another artifact.

rule_text.name: 702.261a
rule_text.rule: Ride is an activated ability of some double-faced cards. “Ride [cost]” means “[cost]: Transform this creature and attach it to target creature you control that doesn't have a Steed enchantment attached to it. As long as this card remains attached to a permanent, you may pay [cost] any time you could cast a sorcery to unattach it from that permanent. Ride only as a sorcery.”

rule_text.name: 702.261b
rule_text.rule: If a Steed is on the battlefield not attached to a permanent, it transforms rather than being put into its owner's graveyard if able. (This is a state-based action. See rule 704.)

rule_text.name: 702.261c
rule_text.rule: The creature a Steed card enchants may be referred to as its “rider”. Effects that refer to a Steed's rider are identical to those that would refer to enchanted creature.

rule_text.name: 702.261d
rule_text.rule: One card (Bonescourge Kazadrak) allows its ride ability to be activated from its owner's graveyard. If this is done, the card will be put onto the battlefield transformed rather than transforming the card.

rule_text.name: 702.261e
rule_text.rule: One card (The Scourgebone Pact) states that its rider "can't dismount". This means a player can't pay [cost] to unattach the Steed from the creature it is attached to. The Steed will still transform back to its front face if it is unattached somehow, such as its rider leaving the battlefield.

rule_text.name: 702.264a
rule_text.rule: Advance is a keyword ability that represents a static ability that functions while the spell with advance is on the stack, and an activated ability. “Advance [cost]” means “You may choose to pay [cost] rather than pay this spell's mana cost. If you do, as the permanent it becomes enters the battlefield, it advances” and “[cost]: This permanent advances. Activate only as a sorcery.”

rule_text.name: 702.264b
rule_text.rule: “Advances” is a designation that has no rules meaning other than to act as a marker that other spells and abilities can identify. The number of times a permanent has advanced is not part of the permanent's copiable values.

rule_text.name: 702.264c
rule_text.rule: If a triggered ability refers to the mana that was spent to advance a permanent, it means the mana used to cast that spell if that ability was triggered by the creature advancing as a result of being cast for its advance ability, the mana used to activate its advance ability if that ability was triggered by the creature advancing as a result of its advanced activated ability resolving, and nothing if it is triggered in some other manner.

rule_text.name: 702.264a
rule_text.rule: Advance is a keyword ability that represents a static ability that functions while the spell with advance is on the stack, and an activated ability. “Advance [cost]” means “You may choose to pay [cost] rather than pay this spell's mana cost. If you do, as the permanent it becomes enters the battlefield, it advances” and “[cost]: This permanent advances. Activate only as a sorcery.”

rule_text.name: 702.264b
rule_text.rule: “Advances” is a designation that has no rules meaning other than to act as a marker that other spells and abilities can identify. The number of times a permanent has advanced is not part of the permanent's copiable values.

rule_text.name: 702.264c
rule_text.rule: If a triggered ability refers to the mana that was spent to advance a permanent, it means the mana used to cast that spell if that ability was triggered by the creature advancing as a result of being cast for its advance ability, the mana used to activate its advance ability if that ability was triggered by the creature advancing as a result of its advanced activated ability resolving, and nothing if it is triggered in some other manner.

mechanics.original_reminder: As this enters, conjure its contents into a shuffled face-up additional library.

rule_text.name: 702.265a
rule_text.rule: Codex is a static ability of some permanents. “Codex — [list of card names]” means “As this permanent enters, conjure cards named [list of card names] and shuffle them into an additional, face up, library.”

rule_text.name: 702.265b
rule_text.rule: The additional library is referred to as “the codex's library” by the permanent with the codex ability that created it.

rule_text.name: 702.265c
rule_text.rule: “This codex's contents” refers to any card that shares a name with a name in the permanent's codex ability, regardless of if that card was conjured by the specific codex.

rule_text.name: 702.265d
rule_text.rule: If a card would be put into the codex's library, that card is put in that library face up.

rule_text.name: 702.265e
rule_text.rule: If a permanent with codex leaves the battlefield, the archived library remains, but is no longer affected by any effects the permanent provided.

rule_text.name: 702.265f
rule_text.rule: Cards are not revealed when they are put into a face up library. Cards can still become revealed even though the cards are already visible.

rule_text.name: 702.265g
rule_text.rule: If another player gains control of a permanent with codex, they will control any effects of the permanent, but will not own the codex's library. This means cards from the codex's library can't go into that player's hand, graveyard, or library, and cards that player owns can't be put into the codex's library. Effects of the codex may still allow them to manipulate or play the cards in that library.

mechanics.original_reminder: If you cast an instant or sorcery spell, activated a nonmana ability, and attacked this turn, enter a renaissance for this game.

rule_text.name: 702.267a
rule_text.rule: Golden age on an instant or sorcery spell represents a spell ability. It means “If you've cast an instant or sorcery spell this turn, activated a nonmana ability this turn, and attacked this turn, and you're not in a renaissance, you're in a renaissance for the rest of the game.”

rule_text.name: 702.267b
rule_text.rule: Golden age on a permanent represents a static ability. It means “Any time you've cast an instant or sorcery spell this turn, activated a nonmana ability this turn, and attacked this turn, and you're not in a renaissance, you're in a renaissance for the rest of the game”

rule_text.name: 702.267c
rule_text.rule: Being in a renaissance is a designation that has no rules meaning other than to act as a marker that other rules and effects can identify. Any number of players may be in a renaissance at the same time.

rule_text.name: 702.267d
rule_text.rule: After a player enters a renaissance, continuous effects are reapplied before the game checks to see if the game state or preceding events have matched any trigger conditions.

rule_text.name: 702.298a
rule_text.rule: Forsake is a static ability that appears on forsake cards that have a secondary set of mana cost and/or power and toughness characteristics. Any time a player could cast a sorcery, they may pay {2} and exile a card with forsake from their hand face down. That player may look at that card as long as it remains in exile. After the current turn has ended, they may cast that card from exile "forsaken." If they do, the alternative set of its mana cost and/or power and toughness characteristics are used. See 751, “Prototype Cards.”

rule_text.name: 702.298b
rule_text.rule: Exiling a card using its forsake ability is a special action, which doesn’t use the stack. See rule 116, “Special Actions.”

rule_text.name: 702.298c
rule_text.rule: If a player owns multiple forsake cards in exile, they must ensure that those cards can be easily differentiated from each other and from any other face-down cards in exile which that player owns. This includes knowing the order in which those cards were put into exile.

rule_text.name: 702.298d
rule_text.rule: If a player leaves the game, all face-down forsake cards that player owns must be revealed to all players. At the end of each game, all face-down forsake cards must be revealed to all players.

rule_text.name: 702.302a
rule_text.rule: Retinue is a triggered ability, and a designation given to a group of permanents, which usually are tokens created by a retinue ability.

rule_text.name: 702.302b
rule_text.rule: "Retinue — [list of P/Ts]" means "When this permanent enters, for each listed P/T, create a red Army creature token with that P/T. Put each token created this way in this permanent's retinue." This list may include entries in the form "X [P/T]". In that case, X tokens are created instead of just one.

rule_text.name: 702.302c
rule_text.rule: As a player declares attacks, if a creature in a retinue or a creature with a retinue attacks, all creatures in that retinue also attack this combat if able. They may attack other players or permanents.

rule_text.name: 702.302d
rule_text.rule: As a player declares blocks, if a creature in a retinue or a creature with a retinue block, all creatures in that retinue also block this combat if able. They may block other creatures.

rule_text.name: 702.302e
rule_text.rule: A permanent can't have more than one retinue. If more permanents are added at a later time, they will be added to the previous retinue, and not a new one.

rule_text.name: 702.302f
rule_text.rule: A permanent can't be in more than one retinue. If it is put into one, it is removed from any retinue it was already in. If it is put into multiple simultaneously, its controller chooses one.

rule_text.name: 702.302g
rule_text.rule: If a permanent would be put into the retinue of a permanent that is itself in a retinue, they are instead put into the same retinue as that permanent.

rule_text.name: 702.302h
rule_text.rule: A retinue will continue to exist even if the permanent that it belongs to is no longer on the battlefield. Certain effects may also create a retinue that belongs to no permanent.

rule_text.name: 702.302i
rule_text.rule: A permanent can't be put into its own retinue.

rule_text.name: 702.304a
rule_text.rule: Lucid appears on some modal instant and sorceries. It represents a static ability that functions while the spell is on the stack. "Lucid" means "If you cast this spell from your hand or from exile, exile it instead of putting it anywhere else as it resolves. As you cast a modal instant or sorcery spell while this card is exiled, you may choose one of this card's modes. If you do, change the text of that spell by adding the chosen mode into one of its bulleted lists and put this card into its owner's graveyard."

rule_text.name: 702.304b
rule_text.rule: If you're applying more than one card with lucid onto a spell, you will put them all into their owner's graveyard and choose the order in which the effects will happen. The new modes will always be added to the end of the list.

rule_text.name: 702.304c
rule_text.rule: The spell has the characteristics of the main spell, plus the rules text found in the chosen mode of the lucid card. This is a text-changing effect (see rule 612, “Text-Changing Effects”). The spell doesn’t gain any other characteristics (name, mana cost, color, supertypes, card types, subtypes, etc.) of the lucid cards. Text gained by the spell that refers to a card by name refers to the spell on the stack, not the card from which the text was copied.

rule_text.name: 702.304d
rule_text.rule: If a mode with an associated cost, such as those found on cards with spree, is added to another spell, this cost will still need to be paid regardless if the new spell has spree.

rule_text.name: 702.304e
rule_text.rule: If a mode without an associated cost is added to a card with spree, the player will be unable to pay its associated cost and unable to choose the mode.

rule_text.name: 702.304f
rule_text.rule: If a mode with star or pawprint symbols is added to a modal spell which does not use them to select modes, the mode may be chosen regardless of those symbols.

rule_text.name: 702.304g
rule_text.rule: If a mode without stars or pawprints is added to a modal spell that does use them to select modes, the mode is not a legal choice.

rule_text.name: 702.307a
rule_text.rule: Stardom is a keyword ability that represents two static abilities, one that functions while the spell with stardom is on the stack, and another that functions while the permanent with stardom is on the battlefield. “Stardom [cost]” means “You may choose to pay [cost] rather than pay this spell's mana cost. If you do, it has base power and toughness 4/4 and is legendary” and “Any time you have priority and this creature is attacking, you may pay [cost]. If you do, this permanent has base power and toughness 4/4 and is legendary. Take this action only once.”

rule_text.name: 702.307b
rule_text.rule: The second ability of stardom is a special action, and its cost can only be modified by abilities that explicitly modify the stardom action.
